memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The LORD said to Moses: 'If anyone sins and is unfaithful to the LORD by deceiving a neighbour about something entrusted to them or left in their care or about something stolen, or if they cheat their neighbour,'" - Lev 6:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Read that carefully. A man deceives his neighbour — and God calls it being unfaithful to the LORD.

Chapter 5 ended by teaching us that wrongs against people are wrongs against God. Chapter 6 opens by demonstrating it. Every offence listed here is horizontal: a deposit denied, an item stolen, a neighbour cheated. Not one of them happened in the tabernacle. All of them happened in the marketplace, the field, the ordinary business of life.

And God files them under unfaithfulness to Him.

This closes the gap many of us maintain between our "spiritual life" and our "real life." We can be devout on Sunday and sharp in business on Monday, warm in prayer and cold with a family member, and imagine these belong to separate categories. God does not recognise the division.

John writes bluntly: Whoever claims to love God yet hates a brother or sister is a liar (1 Jn 4:20). James says that religion God accepts as pure looks after orphans and widows in their distress (Jas 1:27).

Your integrity with people is your integrity with God. There is no third place to keep it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I run two standards — one for church and one for business or home?
2. Is there a person I have dealt with unfairly whom God is bringing to mind?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, forgive me for treating my dealings with people as separate from my walk with You. Make me one person, honest in every room. Amen.
